# Pagination

Marker- and offset-paginated list operations return an `Iterable` that threads
the cursor for you — the list method *is* the paginator, so you loop it directly
with an enhanced `for`:

```java
for (var item : client.folders.listItems(folderId, null)) {
    // use item
}
```

Pass an options object (or `null`) as the final argument. The paginator stops
when the last page is reached. It is re-iterable: each `iterator()` runs an
independent pass over a private copy of your options, so your options object is
never mutated.

## Events

`client.events.stream` follows Box's long-poll event stream: iterating yields the
events after `streamPosition` (`"now"` when null), each once — Box may deliver
an event twice — blocking on a real-time server until Box reports a change. It
lists a fresh server when Box asks it to reconnect, and retries a long poll that
times out; a failed call throws. `close()`, from any thread, stops it:

```java
var events = client.events.stream(null);
while (events.hasNext()) {
    var event = events.next();
    // use event; events.close() (from any thread) to stop
}
```

## Representations (PDF, text, thumbnails)

`client.files.getRepresentationContent` downloads a rendering of a file that Box
generates on demand — a PDF, its extracted text, page images. `repHints` names it
as Box's `X-Rep-Hints` header does; `assetPath` picks one asset of a multi-asset
representation (`"1.png"` for a page) and is `""` for a single-file one. It
blocks while Box generates the representation, up to `maxWait`
(`Runtime.DEFAULT_REPRESENTATION_WAIT` with the three-argument overload), and
throws if Box fails to:

```java
var text = client.files.getRepresentationContent(fileId, "[extracted_text]", "");
```
